notes.note: You can now copy the current tab's URL with a keyboard shortcut. No shortcut is assigned by default, so you can choose your own key combination in **Customize keyboard shortcuts** in Firefox Settings. [Learn more](https://support.mozilla.org/kb/keyboard-shortcuts-perform-firefox-tasks-quickly)
The Themes page in the Add-ons Manager now includes a Classic themes section, with the Proton theme from earlier versions of Firefox, a Firefox OLED theme, and a selection of solid-colored themes.

On [Firefox for Android][1], Extension users now see a more prominent message when an extension has an update pending that requires approval for new permissions or data collection consent.

  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.firefox_beta
On macOS, keyboard shortcuts assigned to Firefox menu items in System Settings now replace the built-in shortcuts for those items.
Browsing history imported from Chrome now includes how often you visited each page, so the sites you use most rank higher in address bar suggestions and shortcuts.

Firefox now supports the `random()` CSS function, which allows authors to introduce randomness into their styles, generating a random value in a given range (with an optional increment) that is usable anywhere that math functions can be specified. [Learn more][1].


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/random

Firefox now supports [nested arbitrary substitution functions][1] in the primary parameters of `var()`, `attr()`, and `env()`; for example, `var(attr(data-theme-prop type(<custom-ident>)))` and `env(var(--safe-area-block-start))`.


  [1]: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#replace-an-arbitrary-substitution-function

Firefox now supports web custom formats in the Async Clipboard API (`navigator.clipboard.read()` and `write()`), letting websites copy and paste their own data formats between pages of the same origin.
Fixed the Developer Tools eyedropper showing the wrong colors after the page is scrolled.
On Firefox for Android, fixed pages that request landscape orientation being saved as shrunken portrait pages when printing or saving to PDF.
Fixed the Windows taskbar staying visible over full-screen Firefox windows after switching back from another application.
Fixed Firefox hanging on macOS 26+ when opening Spotlight with a large number of bookmarks.
Fixed WebRTC video calls with some services sending low-resolution H.264 video since Firefox 158.
Fixed some tabs not being restored after a restart when the saved session referred to a tab group that no longer existed.
Fixed typing with an input method, such as for Japanese or Korean, stopping after the first character in Canva Docs.
Significantly improved rendering performance for `backdrop-filter` on certain Android devices.

system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Beta gets updated 3 times a week and as a consequence, the release notes for the Beta channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports.
Warning: Features listed here may or may not make a final release of Firefox

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development via the [Firefox Trains][1] website or our [@FirefoxBeta][2] Bluesky account. [1]: https://whattrainisitnow.com/beta/ [2]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxbeta.bsky.social
